Who it's for

Skincare routines

The reason most people buy tea tree, and it is usually bought for a specific blemish rather than general use.

Homemade cleaning products

Earns its place in a surface spray, where the medicinal smell is an asset rather than a drawback.

Anyone who wants one practical oil

If you want a single bottle that does something useful rather than smelling nice, this is it.

What people get wrong

Applying it neat to a spot. This is by far the most common tea tree mistake and the fastest route to a sensitivity you then have for life. Dilute to one per cent, even for targeted use.

Using an old bottle on skin. Oxidised tea tree is substantially more likely to cause a reaction than fresh. If it has been open more than a year, keep it for cleaning and buy a new one for skin.

What it won't do

It is not a medicine and we make no claims about what it treats. It is also one of the more frequent causes of contact allergy among essential oils, which is worth knowing before you use it daily.

We describe how our oils smell and how people use them. We don't make medical claims, because essential oils aren't medicine.

Questions about Tea Tree Shield

Can I dab it straight onto a spot?

We would strongly advise against it, even though it is the most commonly given advice online. Neat application is the main way people become sensitised to tea tree. One per cent in jojoba, applied with a cotton bud, is the safer route.

Does it go off?

It oxidises, and oxidised tea tree is noticeably more irritating than fresh. Keep the cap tight, store it cool and dark, and retire it from skin use after about a year.

Is it safe for pets?

No. Tea tree is genuinely toxic to cats and dogs, including as vapour in an enclosed room. If you have pets, do not diffuse it and keep the bottle somewhere they cannot reach.

How long does it keep once opened?

Two to three years stored properly — cool, dark and tightly closed. Distilled oils keep considerably better than cold-pressed citrus.

What dilution should I use on skin?

Lower than most. Genuinely toxic to cats and dogs, including as vapour in a closed room. Dilute to 1% or below on skin; never apply it neat. For general use, dilute into a carrier oil such as jojoba and patch-test on a small area first.

Can I take it internally?

No. None of our oils are food grade and none are sold for internal use. Essential oils are extremely concentrated, and advice to add them to water or food is not advice we endorse.

How quickly will it arrive?

Orders are dispatched from Delhi within two business days and usually arrive within a further three to five, depending on where you are. Shipping is free over ₹999.
